why: Here Judah means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but 2:8 has Shimei meet David at the Jordan on the way back from Mahanaim, much farther south, so no dot is drawn. Bible Atlas draws this Kidron near the coast; the Kidron Valley of 2:37 runs just east of Jerusalem, so no dot is drawn. Here Judah means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 4:25 ("from Dan all the way to Beersheba") Dan is the northern city, which is linked separately as a place, not Jacob's son Dan or his tribe. Here Ephraim, Naphtali, Asher, Issachar, Benjamin and Judah mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 7:21 Boaz is the name of one of the two bronze pillars at the temple porch, not Ruth's husband Boaz. Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but 7:46 places the casting in the Jordan valley between Succoth and Zarethan, farther south, so no dot is drawn. Here Naphtali means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 9:26 the chapter names Edom, the land and its people, not Esau himself; Bible Atlas links Esau because Edom descends from him. The text of 9:18 reads Tamar, a town in the wilderness of Judah; Bible Atlas draws Tadmor (Palmyra) in the Syrian desert, the reading of 2 Chronicles 8:4 and of a Hebrew margin note, so no dot is drawn. Bible Atlas puts the Sea of Reeds far down the Red Sea, but 9:26 means its northern arm, the Gulf of Aqaba by Eloth. Here Israel means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 11:14-17 the chapter names Edom, the land and its people, not Esau himself; Bible Atlas links Esau because Edom descends from him. Here Israel, Moab, Midian and Joseph mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 12:29-30, where Jeroboam sets up a calf Dan is the northern city, which is linked separately as a place, not Jacob's son Dan or his tribe. Here Israel, Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Levi mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Judah means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Judah and Israel mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

In 15:20 Dan is the northern city, which is linked separately as a place, not Jacob's son Dan or his tribe. Tirzah in 15:21 and 15:33 is the town, which is linked as a place, not Zelophehad's daughter Tirzah. Bible Atlas draws this Kidron near the coast; the Kidron Valley of 15:13 runs just east of Jerusalem, so no dot is drawn. Here Judah, Naphtali, Benjamin and Issachar mean the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.
Here Judah means the tribe or people and its land, not the ancestor of that name.

Bible Atlas draws Tishbe in Upper Galilee, but 17:1 calls Elijah a settler of Gilead, east of the Jordan, where tradition places his home. Bible Atlas's Jordan point is near the river's sources in the far north, but the Kerith Brook of 17:3 faces the Jordan farther south, on its middle course, so no dot is drawn.
In 18:12 the text says "the LORD's Spirit". Many Christians read this as the Holy Spirit, while Jewish readers take it as God's own spirit or power; the verse itself does not use that name.
